intro: ばこそ is the ば-form plus the spotlight こそ: it is precisely because of this, and nothing else, that. It is a formal, written-style からこそ. The reason it names is a real fact, usually a motive or a precondition, and the sentence often defends an action that might look harsh or strange from outside.

skills.rule: To insist that a real reason, and only that reason, lies behind something, put the verb in its ば-form and add こそ: 愛すればこそ.
skills.explain:
Build it on the ば-form: 思えばこそ, 信頼していればこそ, 若ければこそ. Nouns and な-adjectives use であればこそ: 健康であればこそ, 親であればこそ. The main clause often ends in のだ / のです, explaining: 子供を愛すればこそ、厳しく叱るのです (it is because I love my children that I scold them hard).

Despite the ば, it is not a condition. The reason is already true; ばこそ adds that it is the very reason. So 明日晴れればこそ cannot mean if it is sunny tomorrow. It also suits motives, judgements and preconditions, not plain physical causes: rain stopping a match is ので, not ばこそ.

The edge: からこそ means the same and is the everyday choice; ばこそ is written, formal or rhetorical. ゆえに names a cause with no spotlight. Note the old idiom ～もあらばこそ meaning there was not even (逃げる暇もあらばこそ: there was no time even to run); it is literary and rare, so recognise it but do not produce it.
patterns: [verb ば-form] こそ、[action / result] のだ

examples.jp: あなたのことを思[おも]え{ばこそ}、こう言[い]っているんです。
examples.en: I am saying this precisely because I care about you.

examples.jp: 子供[こども]を愛[あい]すれ{ばこそ}、厳[きび]しく叱[しか]るのです。
examples.en: It is because I love my children that I scold them so strictly.

examples.jp: 健康[けんこう]であれ{ばこそ}、好[す]きな仕事[しごと]が続[つづ]けられる。
examples.en: Only because you are healthy can you keep doing the work you love.

examples.jp: 仲間[なかま]がいれ{ばこそ}、ここまで頑張[がんば]れた。
examples.en: It is only because I had my friends that I made it this far.

examples.jp: 信頼[しんらい]していれ{ばこそ}、この仕事[しごと]を任[まか]せたのだ。
examples.en: It is precisely because I trust you that I gave you this job.

contrast.note: Same meaning. からこそ is neutral and fine in conversation; ばこそ is formal and literary. In a casual chat, からこそ.
ゆえに states a cause, including logical ones, without emphasis. ばこそ says this exact reason, defending a choice or result.
とあって reports what follows from a special situation as an observer (祭りとあって人が多い). ばこそ explains a motive or precondition from inside.

mistakes.bad: 明日[あした]晴[は]れれ{ばこそ}、海[うみ]に行[い]こう。
mistakes.good: 明日[あした]晴[は]れれ{ば}、海[うみ]に行[い]こう。
mistakes.note: ばこそ is not a condition. For if, use plain ば.

mistakes.bad: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]れ{ばこそ}、試合[しあい]が中止[ちゅうし]になった。
mistakes.good: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]った{ので}、試合[しあい]が中止[ちゅうし]になった。
mistakes.note: A plain physical cause of an event takes ので or から. ばこそ is for motives and preconditions.

mistakes.bad: 好[す]きなら{こそ}、厳[きび]しくするのだ。
mistakes.good: 好[す]きであれ{ばこそ}、厳[きび]しくするのだ。
mistakes.note: なら does not take こそ. A な-adjective or noun uses であればこそ.

skills.tip: Can you swap in からこそ and keep the meaning, and is the tone formal? Then ばこそ, built on the ば-form.
